paragraphs: Lobiani means bean bread and is eaten throughout Georgia, especially for Barbaroba; this meatless bakery-style form keeps the kidney-bean filling and Georgian blue fenugreek distinct from smoked-pork Rachan versions.

Lobiani means bean bread and is eaten throughout Georgia, especially for Barbaroba on December 17. Rachan versions may cook beans with smoked ham or pork fat. This meatless bakery-style version keeps the nationally recognizable kidney-bean filling and Georgian blue fenugreek. This Kwilt version follows the reviewed household adaptation: Choose the widespread meatless form and retain the most culturally specific seasoning, while documenting rather than blending in the distinct Rachan smoked-pork variation.

paragraphs: Ćevapi vary across the Balkans; Bosnian forms commonly use beef or beef and lamb without pork and serve small grilled meat fingers in somun or lepinja with raw onion.

Ćevapi vary across Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Croatia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and neighboring regions. Bosnian forms commonly use beef or beef and lamb without pork and pair them with somun or lepinja and raw onion; ajvar and kajmak are widespread but not universal. This Kwilt version follows the reviewed household adaptation: Use a Bosnian-leaning beef-and-lamb profile within the broader Balkan roster label, authoring lepinja and keeping optional regional condiments visibly separate.
